source: OSCAR v2.0 final (Earth & Space Research, NASA PO.DAAC), daily 0.25 deg total surface current (mean of the top 30 m: geostrophic + Ekman + buoyancy), monthly means of days 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 of each month 2015-2024, native 0.25 deg grid
citation: ESR (2022). OSCAR Third Degree Resolution Ocean Surface Currents, version 2.0 final (0.25 degree, daily). PO.DAAC, CA, USA. doi:10.5067/OSCAR-25F20. Dohan, K. (2017). Ocean surface currents from satellite data. J. Geophys. Res. Oceans 122, 2647-2651, doi:10.1002/2016JC012246
licence: NASA Earth science data, free and open ("OSCAR products are supported by NASA and may be freely distributed"); cite the DOI
attribution: Currents: OSCAR v2.0 (ESR, NASA PO.DAAC), 2015-2024 monthly means
annual_note: annual = mean of the 12 monthly means, only where all 12 months have open water
caveats: OSCAR is a diagnostic model driven by satellite sea level (DUACS), ERA5 winds and SST, not a measurement; it is a top-30 m mean, so it is weaker than the surface skin current and than drifters in narrow jets.
Averaging 60 daily snapshots smooths eddies and meanders: the climatological Gulf Stream and Kuroshio are broader and slower than on any given day.
Within ~1 deg of the equator the geostrophic part is ill-defined; OSCAR uses a special equatorial treatment there.
No data under sea ice: a cell is kept for a month only when >= 80 % of the 60 snapshots are valid; polar seas and coastal cells inshore of the 0.25 deg grid are empty.

grid.registration: grid nodes (native OSCAR 0.25 deg points); row r is at latitude lat0 - r * res_deg, column c at longitude lon0 + c * res_deg; longitudes wrap
grid.encoding: zlib-deflated; u then v, each little-endian int16 stored as two byte planes (all low bytes, then all high bytes); value (m/s) = q * scale; q = -32768 = no data
grid.components: u = eastward, v = northward (true north, not grid north)
